chunks: From Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said:
Allah keeps a believer away from what He dislikes even if he longs for it, just as a man keeps a camel away from a flock it does not belong to.
ai.seo_question: How does Allah protect believers from what they desire but is harmful to them?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the concept of divine protection (yadhub) where Allah prevents a believer from falling into sin or harm, even when the believer desires it. It uses the analogy of a shepherd keeping a stray camel away from his own flock to show that Allah's restraint is an act of care and preservation for the believer.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 25. It has been narrated that Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) said:
Allah keeps a believer away from what He dislikes even if he (the believer) longs for it, just as a man keeps a camel away from a flock it does not belong to.
